title: From the semi-modular to the Malevolent
intro: The Malevolent is PWM’s 2022 semi-modular keyboard synth, an original British design whose analogue circuits are by Future Sound Systems. Like the semi-modulars before it, every section is wired inside so it plays with no cables, and every wire can be replaced at the patch points: here each input prints the source it is normalled to.

timeline.name: ARP 2600
timeline.text: A semi-modular: oscillators, filter, envelopes and amplifiers wired to one another inside, with patch cords to override any of the connections. The Malevolent’s printed normals follow the same idea.

timeline.name: Moog Grandmother
timeline.text: A semi-modular keyboard synth with 32 keys, two oscillators, one filter and an arpeggiator, playable with no cables and patched at the panel.

timeline.name: PWM Malevolent
timeline.text: Two VCOs whose saw, triangle and pulse are mixed by buttons, a 2-pole Sallen-Key multimode filter with separate low-pass, band-pass and high-pass inputs, two ADSRs, a VCA with drive and a drone switch, an LFO, an arpeggiator and a joystick, with 19 inputs and 19 outputs over 32 mini keys.

timeline.name: PWM Mantis
timeline.text: PWM’s next instrument: a hybrid-analogue duophonic synth completing the last design concept of Chris Huggett, the designer of the EDP Wasp and the OSCar.

relatives.name: Moog Grandmother
relatives.text: The same idea in Moog’s hands: a 32-key semi-modular with two oscillators and an arpeggiator, but a 24 dB ladder low-pass, one envelope and a spring reverb.

relatives.name: Behringer Neutron
relatives.text: A desktop semi-modular with two oscillators, two envelopes, overdrive and a multimode filter whose mode is a knob, all on a large patch bay, and no keyboard.

relatives.name: PWM Mantis
relatives.text: From the same maker: a keyboard synth with digital oscillators, a dual analogue filter and patch memory, where the Malevolent is all analogue with none.
